articleBody:
Before purchasing a replacement faucet or dismantling your kitchen sink connections, gathering the right measurements and inspecting your plumbing prevents messy surprises.

- [ ] Sink hole count — Verify whether your sink has one, two, three, or four holes before ordering a new unit.
- [ ] Hole spacing measurement — Check the center-to-center distance between holes to ensure deck plates cover existing openings.
- [ ] Countertop thickness — Confirm your counter thickness matches the maximum mounting shank depth of the faucet.
- [ ] Spout reach and height — Measure distance to upper cabinets and sink basins to prevent splashing or blocked window sills.
- [ ] Under-sink shutoff valve test — Turn both hot and cold valves off completely to confirm they stop water flow without dripping.
- [ ] Supply line connection sizing — Check whether your shutoff outlets use standard 3/8-inch compression or older 1/2-inch fittings.
- [ ] Flexible supply line condition — Note the age and flexibility of existing hoses so you can replace brittle lines.
- [ ] Basin wrench availability — Ensure you have the proper clearance and tools to reach tight mounting nuts behind deep basins.

How to use this checklist:
Work through these items under your sink before buying fixtures. If you find seized shutoffs, corroded threads, or damaged subflooring, bringing in a licensed contractor will save time and prevent leaks.
